net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
The Company recognizes revenue in accordance with FASB Topic 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) .

The Company’s sales are primarily generated from the sale of finished products to customers. Revenue is recognized when the performance obligation is satisfied, and the promised goods have been transferred. Control transfers when the product is shipped or delivered based upon applicable shipping terms. For each contract, the Company considers the transfer of product to be the performance obligation. Although some payment terms may be extended, generally the Company’s payment terms are approximately 15- 30 days. Accordingly, there is no significant financing components to consider when determining the transaction price. The Company elected to treat shipping and handling activities as fulfillment activities, and the related costs are recorded as selling expenses in selling, general and administrative expenses on the Consolidated Statements of Operations.

The Company promotes its products with trade incentives and promotions. These programs include discounts, slotting fees, coupons, rebates, in-store display incentives and volume-based incentives. The trade incentives and promotions are recorded as a reduction to the transaction price based on amounts estimated as being due to customers at the end of the period.

intro.text: Mama’s Creations, Inc. (together with its subsidiaries, the "Company") is a leading marketer and manufacturer of fresh deli-prepared foods, found in over 12,000 grocery, mass, club and convenience stores nationally. The Company’s broad product portfolio, born from MamaMancini’s rich history in Italian foods, now consists of a variety of high-quality, fresh, clean and easy-to-prepare foods to address the needs of both our consumers and retailers. Our vision is to become a one-stop-shop deli solutions platform, leveraging vertical integration and a diverse family of brands to offer a wide array of prepared foods to meet the changing demands of the modern consumer.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the year ended January 31, 2026, the Company earned revenues from two customers representing approximately 38% and 17% of gross sales, respectively.
During the year ended January 31, 2025, the Company earned revenues from one customer representing approximately 44% of gross sales.
During the year ended January 31, 2024 three customers represented approximately 26%, 11%, and 10% o f gross sales, respectively.
For the year ended January 31, 2026, the Company’s gross revenue was concentrated in two customers that accounted for approximately 38 % and 17 % of gross revenue, respectively.
For the year ended January 31, 2025, the Company’s gross revenue was concentrated in one customer that accounted for approx imately 44 % of gross sales .
For the year ended January 31, 2024, the Company’s gross revenue was concentrated in three customers that accounted for approx imately 26 %, 11 % and 10 % of gross sales , respectiv ely.
Having a strong track record of more than 15 years, our retail partners trust our quality and can rely on our service.
We rely on a combination of trademark, copyright and trade secret laws to establish and protect our proprietary rights.
Supply chain disruptions, including supplier instability and single-source dependence, could impair our ability to manufacture and deliver products.

Damage or disruption to our manufacturing or distribution capabilities due to weather, natural disaster, fire, terrorism, pandemic, strikes, the financial and/or operational instability of key suppliers, distributors, warehousing and transportation providers, or brokers, or any other reasons could impair our ability to manufacture or sell our products.
The majority of our business depends on a limited number of principal customers.

Because we depend on a limited number of customers for a significant portion of our sales, a loss of a small number of these customers could materially adversely affect our business and financial condition.
We rely on key personnel and, if we are unable to retain, motivate key personnel, or hire qualified personnel, we may not be able to grow effectively.

The declaration of any future cash dividends is at the discretion of our Board of Directors and depends upon our earnings, if any, our capital requirements and financial position, general economic conditions, and other pertinent conditions.

Variable lease payments that depend on an index or a rate are initially measured using the index or rate at the commencement date, otherwise variable lease payments are recognized in the period incurred.
